summary: Second-application transfer passed on a fresh 20-case subscription/signup cohort with real text entry and first-app non-regression evidence.

core_changes.change: The actor may keep waiting while an operation is visibly running; MAX_UNCHANGED_WAITS = 12 is enforced in code.
Workers accept a per-journey goal and report text_entry from actual helper calls.
Loading evidence anchors on action_attempt so synchronous feedback is retained.
The text helper uses a separate HTTP client so Jev-only budget hooks cannot reject or account Azure helper requests.
An incomplete goal scrolls for below-viewport controls before DONE or BLOCKED.

second_app_binding.setup_time: Not instrumented separately; reported journey medians include actor execution but not implementation time.
second_app_binding.app_specific_fix: After subscription, the persistent confirmation section is brought into view so the user-visible effect and evidence agree.

retained_non_admission_runs.cause: The Jev budget hook rejected Azure helper requests on the shared HTTP client.

retained_non_admission_runs.result: 7/10 defects, 2/10 spurious, 0/10 completed controls, four false passes
retained_non_admission_runs.cause: The actor did not scroll to the persistent review section.
The confirmation body remained below the viewport in clean effect controls.

cp5_prerequisite.note: The original spurious case remains recorded and was not re-judged.

limitations: One of 20 admission journeys ended in a retained execution failure.
The second app is synthetic and loopback-only.
The original CP5 10x economic gate remains unmet; the owner restated the value proposition around latency and throughput.
next_permitted_action: Assess CP7 framework admission and extract only mechanisms demonstrated by both applications.
